newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks close slightly higher on thin volume.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks close slightly higher on thin volume.

text.p: The Athens bourse closed slightly higher on Friday in thin volume after trading narrowly for most of the session and analysts said the market was paying attention to developments in a 16-day farmers' revolt.
The general index closed at 905.86, 0.02 percent higher than Thursday's close of 905.65. Turnover was at 4.731 billion drachmas on volume of 2.53 million shares.

There were some block trades with 35,000 shares of Papastratos trading at 4,600 drachmas. Two block trades of Hellenic Bottling took place, with 50,000 shares trading at 7,285 and 15,000 shares trading at 7,200 drachmas.

"The Hellenic Bottling block trades occured as a result of the company's announcement of the renewal of its contract with the Coca Cola company for another decade," said Nota Zagari, Alpha Trust's fund manager.
"I think this has stabilised Hellenic Bottling company's stocks and has made them a long-term investment," she added.
Press reports said that barricades around Patras and Salonica, in norhtern Greece, have weakened, but, farmers are determined to keep up the blockades in central Greece.
Losers led gainers 82 to 104 with 33 issues unchanged on 219 shares traded. Banks rose 0.81 percent, industrials gained 4.02 percent and construction eased 3.62 percent. Small-caps lost 0.07 percent.
